questions.title: Which company will hold the record for the largest US IPO by a foreign firm as of July 10, 2026?
questions.background: Alibaba's 2014 US initial public offering raised $25 billion, setting the record for the largest US IPO by a foreign company.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official issuer announcements and contemporaneous reporting by reputable news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the company reported as holding the all-time record for the largest US initial public offering by a foreign company as of July 10, 2026. Compare offerings by proceeds raised, not company valuation. An offering whose pricing and share sales have been announced may qualify before exchange trading begins. Accepted Answer Format : The company's commonly used name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major opposing July 7 developments wipe out SK Hynix's valuation buffer above Alibaba's $25.03B record while sharply compressing discount and execution risk ahead of Thursday July 9 pricing. Bearishly, KOSPI plunged -4.91% Tuesday (triggering a 20-minute circuit breaker) on sell-the-news profit-taking despite Samsung's record 89.4T won Q2 profit, dragging SK Hynix down -6.06% to 2,201,000 KRW (KRW/USD 1,528.20)—reducing the gross value of its hard-capped 17.79M new shares (constrained by SK Square's 20% regulatory ownership floor) from $27.24B to $25.62B (+2.37% above $25.03B)—and after Seoul's close U.S. chip stocks tumbled on AI-peak and DeepSeek custom-chip concerns (SOX -4.65%, Micron -4.7%, Sandisk -7.3%, SpaceX ~-7%; Reuters/Straits Times). Bullishly, Bloomberg reported Tuesday afternoon (Stocktwits) that SK Hynix's ADS offering is already oversubscribed multiple times with ~1,000 institutional investors on its marketing call and $7B in cornerstone interest (Baillie Gifford, Coatue, Situational Awareness), prompting books to close early at 4:00 PM NY Wednesday July 8 (Phemex)—cutting delay/downsizing risk to minimal levels, compressing expected ADR pricing discount to ~1.5-2.5% (putting spot-implied proceeds around $25.06B right on Alibaba's $25.03B threshold), and providing a bullish headline into Wednesday's Seoul session. Hierarchical Monte Carlo over 1-2 remaining Seoul sessions, ~6.5% daily volatility, tight discount (~2.2%), slight net negative overnight drift, and ~4% non-price risk shifts our forecast from SK Hynix 0.61 to Alibaba 0.54 / SK Hynix 0.46.

local_articles.snippet: NEW YORK - SK Hynix’s US$28 billion (S$36 billion) US listing is multiple times oversubscribed ahead of pricing on July 9, according to people familiar with the matter. The South Korean memory chip giant’s offering has drawn strong early demand from global long-only funds and technology-focused investors, the people said. About 1,000 institutional investors joined a management marketing call on July 6, the people said. A representative for SK Hynix didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. International Financing Review earlier reported the offering’s subscription level. SK Hynix began marketing the sale on July 6 of 177.9 million American depositary receipts (ADR) valued at about US$28 billion, based on the July 3’s closing price of its common shares in Seoul. questions.background: India and England are scheduled to contest a T20 international series in England.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official match results or contemporaneous AFP reporting identifying the winner of the England–India T20 international series in July 2026. Resolution Timing : Resolve when a team secures an unassailable series lead, or when the series concludes if its winner has not previously been determined. Accepted Answer Format : The country name of the series-winning team.
questions.current_reasoning: Decisive July 7 match result (Khaleej Times, Hindustan Times): England thrashed India by 125 runs in the 3rd T20I at Trent Bridge (England 201/7 behind Phil Salt's 70 and Sam Curran's 41*; India bowled out for 76—their heaviest T20I defeat—as Josh Tongue took 4-28 and Jofra Archer 3-29) to take a 2-0 series lead with only two matches left (July 9 Bristol, July 11 Southampton) following the July 1 Durham rain washout. India is now mathematically eliminated from winning the series (sweeping both remaining games can at best produce a 2-2 draw), so India is removed (0%). England wins the series outright with either a single win or a single rainout across the final two matches (~88% unconditional probability given England's home edge and ~9-10% per-match UK washout risk); combining that with the resolution format specifying the country name of the series-winning team sets optimal strictly proper BSS probability at England 0.92.

questions.title: Which UK university will be identified in nationwide reporting by the end of July 2026 as having investigated the most students for pro-Palestine activism between October 2023 and November 2025?
questions.background: Pro-Palestinian campus protests in Britain have prompted disputes over university disciplinary practices and freedom of expression.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Nationwide comparative reporting by Al Jazeera and Liberty Investigates, drawing on university Freedom of Information disclosures and available by July 31, 2026. Resolution Rule : Resolve to the university with the highest reported number of students subjected to disciplinary investigations for pro-Palestine activism between October 2023 and November 2025 among the universities covered. Investigations need not have resulted in sanctions. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the university.
questions.current_reasoning: Al Jazeera English and Liberty Investigates already launched their 2026 FOI series (to >150 UK universities) in April 2026; in Liberty Investigates' earlier Feb 2025 FOI dataset covering Oct 2023-Aug 2024, University College London led all known UK institutions with 12 students investigated (ahead of Cardiff with 9 by April 2025, King's College London with 7, and LSE with at least 7). UCL also has one of the UK's largest student bodies and a proven track record of disclosing exact student counts rather than redacting under personal-data exemptions. Extending the window through Nov 2025 brings large protest-heavy campuses like Manchester and Oxford (both featured in the April 2026 Al Jazeera/Liberty Investigates Horus surveillance disclosures) into contention, while 40% mass remains across the broad field of other UK universities (SOAS, LSE, Edinburgh, Cambridge, Sheffield, Queen Mary, Leeds, Warwick, Bristol, etc.).

questions.title: Which ownership group will receive NFL owners' approval to buy the Seattle Seahawks in 2026?
questions.background: The Seattle Seahawks are owned by Paul Allen's estate. Allen's will calls for the team to be sold and the assets distributed to charities.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official NFL announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting identifying the purchasing group approved by NFL owners. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the purchasing ownership group in the first sale of the Seattle Seahawks formally approved by NFL owners during 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the purchasing group or the family leading it.
questions.current_reasoning: June 29 Seattle Times coverage citing Bloomberg News reports that first-round bids to buy the Seattle Seahawks were due Monday, June 29 (earlier than previously rumored July 6), that no new potential buyers have emerged beyond the three previously identified groups (Aditya Mittal & Wyc Grousbeck, Todd Boehly, and Vinod Khosla), and that the bidder pool is 'fairly shallow' and 'shrinking' as the record $9B-$10B valuation tests billionaires' cash appetite. Confirming a shallow pool with no newly reported suitors on bid-deadline day concentrates probability mass onto the three active groups (Mittal/Grousbeck 0.30, Boehly 0.25, Khosla 0.23; combined 0.78, up from 0.66), while trimming unmentioned names Apostolopoulos (0.04), Bezos (0.03), and the unannounced mystery-bidder tail (from 23% to 15%).

questions.title: Who will win the 2026 MotoGP German Grand Prix?
questions.background: This question concerns the premier-class main Grand Prix race, not the separate sprint race.
questions.resolution_criteria: Resolve to the rider classified as the winner of the 2026 German Grand Prix main race in the official MotoGP race results. Resolution occurs when the race classification is published. Provide the rider's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: July 3-7 German Grand Prix previews (MotoGP.com, GPBlog, Motorcycles.news, TodoCircuito) bring meaningful rider-fitness updates ahead of Friday July 10 Sachsenring practice. Marco Bezzecchi (trimmed 0.16 -> 0.13) is cleared to race but arrives 'battered and bruised' from his heavy Lap 2 Assen crash, with Aprilia Racing CEO Massimo Rivola publicly noting Bezzecchi 'definitely needs a break' amid four non-scores in five races. Nine-time Sachsenring MotoGP winner Marc Marquez (nudged 0.29 -> 0.31) confirmed his radial-nerve arm surgery six weeks ago ended fears of sudden arm failure and expects a stronger showing on Sachsenring's anti-clockwise, left-hand-dominated layout (where MotoGP.com tabs him double favorite despite Aprilia's 2026 pace). Championship leader and 2023 Sachsenring winner Jorge Martin moves slightly up (0.19 -> 0.20), third-in-standings top Ducati rider Fabio Di Giannantonio ticks up (0.07 -> 0.08), Assen winner Ai Ogura holds at 0.10, and injuries to rivals (Pedro Acosta fresh from carpal tunnel surgery, Maverick Vinales shoulder weakness, Johann Zarco and Fermin Aldeguer out) trim the outsider field to 18% (Raul Fernandez, 2024 winner Bagnaia, Alex Marquez, Acosta).

questions.title: Whom will Donald Trump endorse in the 2026 Republican primary for Tennessee's Ninth Congressional District?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : as established by Trump's public statements or contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution Date : ahead of the August 6, 2026 primary. Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the candidate's first and last name.
questions.current_reasoning: Following Tennessee's Trump-backed May 7, 2026 mid-decade redistricting of TN-09 after Louisiana v. Callais, exactly four Republicans qualified for the August 6 primary: State Sen. Brent Taylor, State Rep. Todd Warner, Charlotte Bergmann, and Jeremy Thompson. Taylor launched minutes after the map passed, immediately self-funded $1 million, and locked up endorsements from both U.S. Senators Marsha Blackburn and Bill Hagerty (who called him 'exactly who President Trump needs'), House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, and 50+ Tennessee GOP officials. Trump routinely aligns with leadership and clear frontrunners in newly drawn GOP seats ahead of early voting (July 17), making Brent Taylor an overwhelming favorite over Warner and Bergmann.
